chapter_theme: The dawning of knowledge (அறிவுதயம்): to know oneself is to come to no harm, and the self so known is knowledge in form, taught by Nandi's grace. Knowledge has no birth and no death and knows itself; passing beyond the world's knowing and not-knowing, the knower finds the Lord in the heart, ends the search for the distant lamp and, the malam removed, abides as Siva with no more birth.
structure_note: Self-knowledge frames the chapter (2355, 2366, 2369). Between them run the verses on அறிவு, most built on one repeated word: knowledge as one's form (2357), as unborn and self-knowing (2358), as passing beyond knowing and not-knowing (2361 to 2363), and as the heart of the wise where the Lord stays (2364). 2367 and 2368 are linked end to beginning by தேடுகின்றேன்.

2355.reading: Knowing oneself, one comes to no harm; not knowing oneself, one ruins oneself; once one knows the knowledge by which one knows oneself, one stays worshipping oneself.
2355.nuance: தன்னை (oneself) opens every line. தன்னையே அர்ச்சிக்க, worshipping oneself, is traditionally taken as worshipping the Lord found as or within one's own self, not as self-regard; the verse does not name the Lord, so that reading comes from the rest of the chapter.

2356.reading: There, as all the mighty great gods bowed, saying that Siva sat on the lion throne, she of the full, rich hair, her conch bangles and anklets sounding at once, said 'Praise'.
2356.nuance: அங்கே (there) does not say where. Placed after 2355 it is taken as the inner scene that opens once the self is known, Siva enthroned and Shakti (பொங்குஆர் குழலி) praising him; read plainly it is a picture of the Lord's court.

2357.reading: Nandi graciously taught me, who did not know it, that knowledge is my form; realising through grace that knowledge is my form, I remained as one whose form is knowledge.
2357.nuance: அறிவு வடிவு (knowledge as form) opens every line. Whose form it is goes unsaid: the self's, as Siddhanta takes the soul to be of the nature of knowing, or the Lord's. Sengalvaraya cites Tiruppugazh 1019, which speaks of knowledge as a holy body beyond knowing and not-knowing. The last word அருந்திருந்தானே is odd (see source issues).

2358.reading: Knowledge has no destruction and no making; knowledge has no support but knowledge; the ends of the Vedas proclaim that knowledge itself knows knowledge.
2358.nuance: ஆதாரம் here is the plain word 'support', not the bodily centres. மறை ஈறுகள் (the ends of the Vedas) are taken as the Upanishads, so the verse claims their authority for knowledge that is self-luminous.

2359.reading: Above the fine flower of the flower one examines there are sixteen spreading petals; there, pure knowledge became Siva's bliss and, as knowledge that had gone beyond, he stayed in union.
2359.nuance: The sixteen-petalled flower is usually taken as a lotus of the yogic body, commonly placed at the throat, though 'above the flower' may point higher. போய அறிவு (knowledge that has gone) is read as knowledge whose separate knowing has ceased. Who is joined (புணர்ந்திருந்தான்) is not said.

2360.reading: Among those who stood firm I spoke of how I had stood intent in the wondrous grace that came; the First One came like gold, I clung to his praised holy form, and he said, 'You are great.'
2360.nuance: The syntax is compressed and முன்னிநின்றாமை and மாயத்து (wondrous, or of maya) are unclear. The scene is taken as the Lord coming in a golden form, perhaps as guru, and acknowledging the devotee; the plain sense of the last two lines is fairly sure, the first two are not.

2361.reading: Know knowledge as knowledge and love; this is how knowledge is known as knowledge; when knowledge is known as knowledge the powers beginning with anima come; Nandi knew knowledge as knowledge.
2361.nuance: அறிவுஅறிவாக opens every line and can mean knowing the knower as knowledge, or knowing (the Lord) as knowledge through knowledge. The command to love (அன்பு செய்மின்) sits beside knowing, not after it. அறிந்தணன் may be அறிந்தனன் (knew) or contain அணன் (one who is near).

2362.reading: The world cries 'knowledge, knowledge', yet no one knows what knowledge and ignorance are; if one passes beyond knowledge and ignorance and becomes knowledge, that is the fine way of knowledge and ignorance.
2362.nuance: The last line, அறிவுஅறியாமை அழகியவாறே, may be plain ('that is the fine way') or ironic ('how fine, this knowing and not-knowing'). The verse's point is that true knowledge is not the opposite of ignorance but lies past both the world's knowledge and its ignorance.

2363.reading: He who removes knowing and not-knowing, when the senses cease and he becomes himself everywhere, stands as knowledge within them, as knowledge made dense; he is Siva too.
2363.nuance: The subject can be Siva, who clears away the soul's knowing and not-knowing, or the freed soul, who, the senses ceased, becomes everywhere and so is Siva too. சிவனும் ஆமே (is Siva as well) leans toward the second, but the verse allows both.

2364.reading: The heart of those with knowledge is the wide world; the heart of those with knowledge is rare austerity; and the first Lord stays there, with the heart of those with knowledge and in it.
2364.nuance: அறிவுடையார் நெஞ்சு opens every line. அகலிடம் (the wide earth) makes the knower's heart as large as the world, holding all; the verse then makes it the place of austerity and of the Lord.

2365.reading: Being Vishnu and the Lord of the flower too, the first cause of the womb in the good land of the body, far and near, he stands as sweet sugarcane and nectar and tastes sweet.
2365.nuance: மாயன் and மலரோன் are Vishnu and Brahma: the one Lord takes their roles. காயநன்னாட்டுக் கருமுதல் may be the first cause of every embryo in the body, or the root seed within the body. Sengalvaraya cites Tiruvasagam and Appar for Siva as sweeter than cane juice; the sugarcane image is shared Saiva devotional language.

2366.reading: All this time I did not know myself; once I knew myself I knew nothing else; knowing myself and never letting go of that abiding, he questions me through myself.
2366.nuance: ஏதும் அறிந்திலேன் can mean that nothing else remained to be known, or that the knower no longer knows objects at all. The last line, என்னையிட்டு என்னை உசாவுகின்றானே, is obscure: 'he' is taken as the Lord within, who inquires of the self by the self.

2367.reading: The lamp of maya stays a while and goes out; the pure lamp stays and sends out its flame; the lamp of the body stays and smoulders; I am the one who seeks the distant lamp.
2367.nuance: Three lamps are set against a fourth. The pure lamp is taken as knowledge and the distant lamp (சேய விளக்கு) as Siva, but the verse does not say so. The last word தேடுகின்றேனை (me who seeks) hangs and is completed by 2368, which opens with தேடுகின்றேன்.

2368.reading: I search the eight directions and the two besides; I look for the feet of the one who owns all good; I sing that the Supreme is my aid; I join him with a mind that never fails.
2368.nuance: The two beyond the eight directions are taken as above and below, so the search is everywhere. Four verbs ending in -கின்றேன் give the stages: search, look, sing, join. குறையாமனைத்தாலே is read as குறையா மனத்தாலே, with an unfailing mind.

2369.reading: Those who came forth first in the Lord's first play, to whom afterwards the great malam came, remove it, know themselves, abide in their ancient Lord and become Siva, and birth does not come again.
2369.nuance: விளையாட்டு (play) is the Lord's sport of creation. பின்னை பெருமலம் வந்தவர் reads as if the malam came after the souls; Siddhanta, as in 2401 (தன் ஆதி மலம்), holds the soul's malam to be beginningless, so பின்னை may mean 'then' rather than 'later'. The close draws the chapter back to its start: knowing oneself ends birth.

links.note: 1512 defines Saivam as knowing oneself and reaching Siva; 2355 opens the chapter on knowledge with the same claim from the other side: not to know oneself is ruin.
2355 states the rule that knowing oneself brings no harm; 2366 tells it as the speaker's own history, from long not knowing to a knowing after which nothing else is known.

The Kural sets understanding against the folly (பேதைமை) that is birth. Tirumular says the knowledge that frees lies beyond both the world's knowledge and its ignorance, so the line falls not between them but past them.
Both make understanding a kind of total possession: the Kural says those with it have everything, Tirumular that their heart is the wide world itself and the place where the first Lord stays.

source_issues: 2358 line 1 reads அழிவில்aல with a stray Latin letter; read அழிவில்லை.
2357 line 4 ends அருந்திருந்தானே, which gives no clear sense; perhaps அமர்ந்திருந்தானே or அறிந்திருந்தானே.
2368 line 4 குறையாமனைத்தாலே is probably குறையா மனத்தாலே.
2360 lines 1 and 2 (மன்னிநின் றாரிடை வந்தருள் மாயத்து முன்னிநின் றாமை) are obscure and may be corrupt.
